transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Friday, September 18. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. 'In talks with payment platforms to ensure UPI fee not passed on to consumers': Government. The government is currently in talks with payment platforms to ensure that merchant fees do not get passed on to consumers. Starting from October fifteenth, officials will closely monitor this situation to protect consumers. They also reassured that merchants will not incur additional GST costs once the MDR is implemented. This initiative aims to support more domestic players in the market and encourage innovation. Four days after DHS' 'Mr Singh' post, Sikh trucker stabbed in US. A Sikh truck driver was brutally stabbed seventeen times in Wyoming. This attack occurred just four days after a controversial US government post. Sikh Americans are demanding a full investigation into the assault. They want authorities to determine if hate played a role in the incident. 'My biggest bet would surely be the doubles': Neha on India's TT medal hopes at Asiad. India's table tennis team has moved from being satisfied with a close loss to China to entering the Asian Games with a world No. 3 men's doubles pair. Neha Aggarwal Sharma believes the change in mindset is visible, but says India still needs another generation to consistently challenge China, Japan and Korea. She also identifies mixed doubles, men's and women's doubles as India's genuine medal chances and discusses Manika Batra's absence. New Green Card rules from September 18: Full list of categories affected. Effective September 18, the USCIS will enforce new public charge regulations for Green Card applicants. These updated guidelines impose stricter financial evaluations and recognize a broader range of public benefits. This modification impacts family and employment-based Green Card submissions lodged from that date forward. Any applications submitted before September 18, 2026, will adhere to the previous criteria, while some applicant groups will still be exempt from these changes. 'I'm a ghost': Indian athlete details Asian Games mess, later deletes video. Sanyal, a bronze medallist at the Asian Championships in China in January 2026, travelled from London to Nagoya via Mumbai and Singapore. But his problems began after he reached Japan, where he said he was made to wait for hours at different facilities as officials struggled to clear him and assign him a room. Flowers at 10,600ft: World's highest twin fields unveiled in Leh. On Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 76th birthday, Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena inaugurated the world's highest and India's largest twin flower fields in Leh, at an altitude of 10,600ft, on Thursday as part of the administration's efforts to diversify agriculture, build skills and create new livelihood opportunities in the Union Territory. Tata group dispute: Panel sought 5-year term for Chandrasekaran early September. About three weeks after N Chandrasekaran announced that he would not seek reappointment, Tata Sons' nomination and remuneration committee (NRC) unanimously urged him to reconsider and recommended a fresh five-year term for him. Florida man hit with $700K fines as city moves to raze inherited home. Javis Sims inherited his childhood home in Boynton Beach in 2009 and says he has spent thousands trying to restore it. With code fines exceeding $700,000, the vacant property was declared unsafe and uninhabitable in 2022. The city says demolition is now required, while Sims continues seeking help to save his house from demolition. Kentucky farmer's $3M find: 800+ rare coins unearthed in field. A Kentucky farmer discovered over 800 Civil War-era gold and silver coins. This extraordinary hoard, valued at more than three million dollars, was found buried. The collection included rare 1863 Double Eagle gold coins, highly prized by collectors. Historical context suggests the coins were hidden during the dangerous Civil War period. Centre agrees to lower cut-off for NEET-SS admission. Nudged by Supreme Court to reduce the cut-off percentile for admission to super specialty medical courses to fill around 2,000 vacant seats, Centre Thursday told the court that the qualifying percentile for NEET-SS may go from the existing 50th to 30th for the proposed special stray vacancy round, to be conducted soon, reports Amit Anand Choudhary. Assam's 'Iron Lady' becomes first woman to lead CRPF's elite CoBRA unit. Sanjukta Parashar, renowned as the Iron Lady of Assam, has made her mark as the first female Inspector General to lead the elite CoBRA unit of the CRPF. With a commendable background in national security and field postings, her historic appointment signifies a groundbreaking advancement for women in India's defense forces, showcasing that roles in frontline combat leadership are now within reach for women. Leaking cabins, hotel shortages: Asian Games face logistical problems and typhoon fears. The 20th Asian Games will bring together more than 17,000 athletes and officials, including Olympic and world champions. The Games are being held mainly in the port city of Nagoya and across the wider Aichi prefecture, with competition running until October 4.

transcript.title: Business and markets
transcript.text: Moving to business, the economy and the markets. Shares to buy or sell: Chandan Taparia of Motilal Oswal recommends three stocks to buy today - 18 September 2026. The Indian stock market is set to open flat on September 18, with mixed global cues. Nifty 50 is staying within a range, while Bank Nifty shows selling pressure after failing to maintain higher levels. Gold, US Treasuries surge as crude oil slide eases inflation concerns. Gold rebounds after three days of losses as lower oil prices ease inflation concerns and Treasury yields retreat Mutual funds are avoiding big trades in India's new closing auction , here's why. Mutual funds are limiting the trades they route through the auction, preferring transactions where an adverse execution price would have a limited impact on a scheme's net asset value. Insurance stocks gain on expectations of lower distributor commissions. Life and general insurance shares gained amid expectations that Irdai could lower commissions paid to distributors, particularly banks, potentially reducing distribution costs. Fed hike tests domestic muscle. Can markets hold the line?. DIIs bought in all 10 previous Fed rate-hike months marked by foreign selling, yet Nifty fell in seven. September puts that support to the test again. Thursday's listings: 6 IPOs take the stage in record debut-day rush. Five of the six companies ended above their issue prices, led by Karamtara Engineering, as a record number of mainboard firms listed on the stock exchanges in a day India's textile exports up around 10 percent on year in first five months of FY27. Powered by Capital Market VVDN Technologies readies for rupees 4,000-5,000 crore IPO. VVDN Technologies' listing plan comes as India's public-market fundraising window has opened up, with IPOs, qualified institutional placements and block deals picking up simultaneously. NSE IPO subscribed 43 percent on the first day of bidding, QIBs' share 19 percent. The rupees 22,560 crore IPO received bids for 38 million shares against 88.6 million on offer, with the non-institutional investor portion subscribed 72 per cent Top 5 breakout stocks to buy today by Sumeet Bagadia: Tata Investment, Kaynes, CDSL; check stop loss, target price. Breakout stocks to buy: Sumeet Bagadia recommends five breakout stocks to buy today , Tata Investment Corporation, Paradeep Phosphates, Welspun Living, Kaynes Technology India, and CDSL. INR settles almost flat; Outflows of foreign funds and global trade uncertainties keep rupee under pressure. The Indian rupee, which slipped below the 96 level in intraday trade, ended Thursday's session with a loss of just 3 paise at 95.94 (provisional) against the US dollar, paring initial losses. The rupee ended almost flat amid a slight fall in the dollar index and crude oil prices, which supported investor sentiment despite global geopolitical volatility. The local currency, however, stayed under pressure due to outflows of foreign funds and global trade uncertainties after the House of Representatives cleared a law authorising President Donald Trump to impose up to a 100 per cent tariff on India and other countries importing Russian oil. Indian shares swung between gains and losses on Thursday before ending on a mixed note. Nifty faces a crucial test on Friday: Will recovery continue or support levels give way?. The price action resulted in the formation of a bullish-bodied candle with an upper shadow, indicating profit booking at higher levels. NIIT and SPJIMR launch Professional Certificate in FinTech Operations. NIIT, a leading skills and talent development corporation and Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan's S.P. Jain Institute of Management and Research (SPJIMR) have announced the launch of a Professional Certificate in FinTech Operations, designed to prepare students, graduates and early-career professionals for roles in India's digital financial services ecosystem. SPJIMR is one of India's leading business schools, ranked #26 globally and #2 in India by the Financial Times Masters in Management 2026 ranking. All-out war at Bombay House over Chandra. Tata Sons' board reappointed its executive chairman, N Chandrasekaran, for five years. DoubleLine's Gundlach Warns of Fiscal Crisis in Next Recession. DoubleLine Capital chief executive Jeffrey Gundlach warned that the next US downturn could trigger a debt crisis that sends long-term Treasury yields sharply higher , defying decades of conventional wisdom that bonds will always serve as safe haven during times of economic strife. Hero Motors IPO subscribed 3.36 times. The offer received bids for 29.80 crore shares as against 8.86 crore shares on offer. Russian crude hard to replace: Refiners. Indian refiners face challenges replacing Russian crude imports due to new US legislation. Treasuries Gain as Oil Retreat Shores Up Confidence in Warsh Fed. US Treasuries rose as oil price declines and gains for UK government bonds reinforced improving sentiment after the Federal Reserve's interest-rate hike and pledge to throttle inflation. LG Electronics enters chest freezer segment in India. LG Electronics India announced its entry into the chest freezer category in India with the launch of its Convertible Chest Freezer range. Marking a significant expansion of LG's refrigeration portfolio, the new range brings LG's expertise in cooling technology to the evolving cold-storage requirements of businesses across retail, HoReCa, dairy, ice cream, pharma and food storage along with home consumption. Moon crater bigger than Rome's Colosseum found. Scientists have discovered a massive crater on the Moon that formed after an asteroid or comet fragment struck the lunar surface in 2024. GLOBAL-MARKETS/ (WRAPUP 5, PIX):GLOBAL MARKETS-World stocks rebound, Treasury yields retreat after Fed, BoE decisions Nifty closes above 23,250 as selective buying offsets rate hike concerns. The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 3.75 percent -4 percent , its first hike since 2023. The central bank's projections also kept the possibility of another rate increase this year on the table, with the latest projections showing a range of views among policymakers. Believed to date to around 300 A.D., the 2.6-by-3-inch fragment describes the dramatic episode involving Odysseus, Helios and the sun god's sacred cattle. More than six months after the start of the Iran war, JPMorgan Chase and Co.'s oil analysts are stating what many traders have been saying privately for some time: the path to the end of the war is increasingly impossible to predict.

transcript.text: Now to your money — taxes, savings and personal finance. Is Punjab heading towards UPS-like pension scheme? Here's what its notification suggests. This comprehensive review will assess both the administrative and financial aspects necessary for effective implementation while also drawing insights from successful practices in other states. A revised pension structure is set to be proposed following this in-depth analysis. Mutual funds with the highest BSE exposure: Could we see a major reshuffle after NSE's listing? Experts weigh in. The Employees Provident Fund Organisation has introduced a new wage ceiling of rupees 25,000, which will directly influence the contributions made by both employees and employers to the provident fund. Furthermore, subscribers of the Employees Pension Scheme can expect an increase in their monthly pension benefits. EPFO Form 10C to claim pension benefits: Who can apply? The EPF wage ceiling limit has been increased to rupees 25,000 with effect from September 17, 2026. However, this does not mean that every employee will experience a lower take home pay. This is dependent on many factors like how much EPF contribution has been now, and others. Read the article. UPI new rules from Oct 15: Will your festive shopping bill get more expensive?. Retailers may raise prices or reduce discounts this festive season as a new 0.4 percent fee on UPI transactions over rupees 2,000 takes effect from October 15. Although the charge cannot be directly passed to consumers, businesses may still adjust final prices accordingly. Monthly versus quarterly interest credit: You might be losing out on money in your savings bank account - here's how. While many banks credit the savings account interest quarterly, there are some that credit the amount monthly. Basically, monthly interest credit means getting the interest earned on a savings account credited to the account each month. So, every month you could see a slightly higher amount than the previous month. Mutual fund analysis: From AMC behaviour to manager style, key checks you should make before putting your money.
